prompt: In this course's lab, what writes the replies that `pl check` counts?
hint: Read the section's warning about the model.

choices.text: A Python stand-in written for the course
choices.why: Right. The arithmetic is real; the behaviour is the course's.

choices.text: A small open language model that `lab.sh` downloads the first time it runs
choices.why: The lab needs no network and downloads nothing.

choices.text: Recordings of a commercial model's answers
choices.why: No model produced any reply in this lab.

choices.text: The person who labelled the test set
choices.why: That person wrote the expected answers, not the replies.

prompt: A reply is not valid JSON. How many of the checks after `json` can it pass?

choices.text: All of them, if the content is right
choices.why: The harness cannot read fields out of text it could not parse.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Right: a reply that fails one check fails every check after it.

choices.text: Only `category` and `urgency`
choices.why: Those come last and need the parsed object.

choices.text: Only `fields`
choices.why: `fields` needs the JSON parsed first.

prompt: Why does the lab use a stand-in rather than calling a real model?

choices.text: Because a real model would score too well for the lessons to have anything to show
choices.why: Real models fail too; that is not the reason given.

choices.text: It costs nothing, answers the same way every run, and fails on purpose
choices.why: Right: free, repeatable, and with something to find.

choices.text: Because the harness cannot talk to a real one
choices.why: `model.py` is the one place to change to point it at one.

choices.text: To keep the course's numbers secret
choices.why: Everything is in `lab.sh`, in the open.

prompt: The bare prompt's reply to `t01` said `Type: Payment`. What was wrong with it?

choices.text: The model misread the message and sorted a payment problem as something else
choices.why: It is about a payment; the content was right.

choices.text: Nothing a program could parse: its own fields and its own words
choices.why: Right. The prompt left all three to the model.

choices.text: It was too long
choices.why: Length was not the problem here.

choices.text: It was cut off by `max_tokens`
choices.why: `stop: end` says it finished on its own.

prompt: Asking for JSON in words, how many of the forty replies failed the `json` check?
Most of the thirteen `json` failures under `v2-json.txt` had the right content. What was wrong with them?

choices.text: Something around the JSON: a code fence or a sentence before it
choices.why: Right. The description never said what may come around the object.

choices.text: Single quotes instead of double
choices.why: Neither reply used single quotes.

choices.text: A missing field
choices.why: All three fields were there.

choices.text: Labels in capital letters
choices.why: The labels matched the lists.

prompt: `pl compare` reports `fixed 13, broken 1` between v2 and v3. Which messages carry evidence about whether the examples helped?
hint: A message that passed both times says nothing about the difference.

choices.text: All forty
choices.why: The 23 that passed both times and the 3 that failed both times cannot tell the prompts apart.

choices.text: The fourteen whose result changed
choices.why: Right. That is what the sign test is computed on.

choices.text: Only the thirteen it fixed
choices.why: The one it broke counts against it, and belongs in the test.

choices.text: The 36 that pass under v3
choices.why: Most of those passed under v2 as well.

prompt: The test that asks how often a fair coin would split the changed results at least as unevenly is the ___ test.
hint: Its name is about which way each one moved.

prompt: A study found few-shot gains survived even when the example labels were wrong. What does that suggest the examples were mostly teaching?
hint: If the labels were wrong, the gain did not come from the labels being right.

choices.text: The right answer for each kind of message
choices.why: Wrong labels would then have hurt much more.

choices.text: Nothing; the gain was noise
choices.why: It was measured across many tasks.

choices.text: The format and the labels
choices.why: Right. Shape and vocabulary carried much of the effect.

choices.text: How to reason step by step
choices.why: The examples showed only inputs and answers.

prompt: Why did adding examples move `t37`, a late order, from delivery to billing?

choices.text: The examples changed the list of labels the model was allowed to use
choices.why: The list was the same in both prompts.

choices.text: It looks like the first one, so it took that one's label
choices.why: Right: likeness to an example moves a message towards that example's label.

choices.text: Billing is first in the list
choices.why: It was first in v2 as well, where `t37` was right.

choices.text: The message mentions money
choices.why: It does not.

prompt: Which example teaches the model the most, for its tokens?
hint: Where would the model go wrong without help?

choices.text: *I can't log in*, labelled account, since it is the commonest message
choices.why: The model sorts that correctly without an example.

choices.text: A refund for a returned book
choices.why: Right: it sits where billing and returns meet.

choices.text: Any message, provided it is short
choices.why: Length is not what makes an example useful.

choices.text: A copy of a message from the test set
choices.why: That inflates the score instead of teaching.

prompt: Why should an example never also be a test case?
hint: What does the model do with a message it has just been shown the answer to?

choices.text: The harness refuses a message that appears in two files and stops the run
choices.why: It does not; nothing would stop you.

choices.text: It costs twice the tokens
choices.why: The cost is not the problem.

choices.text: It is answered by copying, so the score flatters the prompt
choices.why: Right. Lesson 11 measures how far that inflates a score.

choices.text: Examples have to be invented rather than taken from real messages
choices.why: The section recommends real traffic, cleaned.

prompt: The prompt went from 69 tokens to 229 with three examples. How many tokens does each call now pay for the examples and their tags?
Which of these are reasons the section gives for choosing examples carefully? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Every example pulls answers towards its own label
choices.why: Yes: balance matters.

choices.text: Examples are paid for on every call
choices.why: Yes: they are part of every prompt.

choices.text: A model ignores examples after the third
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: Invented examples are cleaner than real messages
choices.why: Yes, and that is the problem: they teach nothing about messy input.

prompt: One example carried `"order": "4471"`. What happened to the forty replies?
hint: Look at `t04`, a customer who cannot log in.

choices.text: Only the replies about orders gained the field
choices.why: `t04` has no order and gained it too.

choices.text: All forty carried the same order number
choices.why: Right. The model had no value of its own, so it copied the one it was shown.

choices.text: The model ignored the field
choices.why: `fields` failed on all forty.

choices.text: They stopped being valid JSON
choices.why: `json` passed on all forty.

prompt: Which check caught the copied order number, and why only that one?
hint: Which check looks for fields nobody asked for?

choices.text: `json`, because the extra field broke the syntax
choices.why: The JSON was valid.

choices.text: `category`, because the order number replaced the category
choices.why: The category was still there.

choices.text: `fields`: it refuses fields nobody asked for
choices.why: Right. A check that only looked for the fields it needed would have passed all forty.

choices.text: None; it was found by reading
choices.why: The check reported 0 passes.

prompt: Why is a defect in an example easy to miss in a demo and loud in a test set?
hint: How many replies does it touch?

choices.text: Demos use a different model
choices.why: Same model, same prompt.

choices.text: It is copied into every answer, and one answer read alone looks deliberate
choices.why: Right: forty out of forty is loud; one out of one looks like a feature.

choices.text: Test sets use stricter models
choices.why: The checks are stricter, not the model.

choices.text: It only appears at high temperature
choices.why: These runs were at temperature 0.

prompt: What does the section recommend to stop examples teaching the wrong thing? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Vary whatever should vary between answers
choices.why: Yes, or every summary starts the same way.

choices.text: Remove names, order numbers and dates
choices.why: Yes: what belongs to one customer leaks into the rest.

choices.text: Check strictly for unexpected fields
choices.why: Yes: that is what caught the order number.

choices.text: Write the examples in a different format from the description, for variety
choices.why: The opposite: an example that disagrees with the description wins.

prompt: Put the three prompts of this lesson in order of how many replies passed every check, fewest first.
items: The prompt that asks for JSON

prompt: Match each change to what it fixed or caused in this lesson.

pairs.left: Asking for JSON and listing the labels
pairs.right: The model's own field names and words
The code fences and sentences around the JSON

pairs.left: An order number left in one example
pairs.right: An extra field in every reply
A late order sorted as billing

right_distractors: Replies cut off in the middle

prompt: A colleague adds a fourth example and the score goes from 36 to 37 of 40. What would you want to see before keeping it?
hint: One message is very little evidence, and an example has a cost.

choices.text: Nothing: a higher score is better
choices.why: One message can move for reasons unrelated to the change.

choices.text: Which messages changed, whether any broke, and what the extra tokens cost on every call
choices.why: Right: `pl compare`, and `pl tokens`.

choices.text: A longer example
choices.why: Length is not evidence.

choices.text: The same run again at temperature 0
choices.why: At temperature 0 the stand-in gives the same answers again; that proves nothing new.
